title: Modular Recon Tool
summary: A modular Python reconnaissance CLI that combines WHOIS and DNS enumeration, passive subdomain discovery, TCP port scanning, banner collection, technology detection, and structured security reporting in one workflow.
fullDescription: Modular Recon Tool automates common information-gathering tasks used during authorized security assessments. Its modular command-line workflow allows individual reconnaissance checks to be executed separately or combined into a complete scan, with results consolidated into structured TXT or HTML reports.
caseStudyContent:
PROBLEM
The reconnaissance phase of a security assessment commonly involves several separate commands, tools, public data sources, and manually organized results. This makes the process repetitive and can produce inconsistent reporting.

SOLUTION
Modular Recon Tool provides one Python command-line workflow for passive information gathering and explicitly authorized active reconnaissance. Users can select individual modules or run the complete workflow, while each result is collected into a consistent report.

VERIFIED CAPABILITIES
  • WHOIS information gathering
  • DNS record enumeration
  • A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, CNAME, and SOA record collection
  • Passive subdomain discovery
  • Certificate Transparency data collection through crt.sh
  • Passive DNS information through AlienVault OTX
  • Subdomain normalization and de-duplication
  • Threaded TCP connect port scanning
  • Configurable port lists
  • Configurable connection timeout
  • Service-name identification
  • Banner collection from discovered open services
  • Basic web technology detection
  • Header, cookie, and HTML signature analysis
  • Individual module execution
  • Complete workflow execution
  • Logging and verbosity controls
  • TXT report generation
  • HTML report generation
  • Docker support
  • Graceful handling of timeouts, unavailable services, DNS failures, and API rate limits

ENGINEERING DECISIONS
  • Each reconnaissance technique is isolated in its own Python module.
  • Modules return structured results for centralized reporting.
  • The port scanner uses Python sockets and concurrent workers.
  • Passive subdomain sources reduce unnecessary direct interaction with the target.
  • Individual module failures do not terminate the complete workflow.
  • Centralized logging supports normal and debug output.
  • Reports are available in readable TXT and HTML formats.
  • Docker provides a portable execution option.

OUTCOME
The project demonstrates practical Python development, network programming, public-data API integration, command-line interface design, concurrent execution, structured reporting, error handling, Docker packaging, and responsible security-tool development.
ethicalDisclaimer: This tool is intended only for education and explicitly authorized security testing. Active reconnaissance must only be performed against systems the user owns or has written permission to assess.
